_comment: CANONICAL cross-repo fixtures for the MeSH-ERIC crosswalk (§3.3).
The thesaurus fragments below are copied from the real shipped snapshot, and the
cases were chosen because they demonstrate why this feature must present
- MeSH `Mindfulness` has no ERIC descriptor. ERIC's `Metacognition` lists
Mindfulness as a Use-For synonym, having folded the cognitive-psychology
sense of the word into it. The strongest available signal therefore yields a
suggestion that is conceptually WRONG for mindfulness-as-meditation.
- MeSH `Asthma` folds into ERIC's `Diseases` the same way. Searching ERIC's
`Diseases` for asthma research would be useless.
Hence the tiers: a label match is strong, a synonym match is only likely, and an
inverted-heading head match is merely possible. Every match carries its evidence.

headCases.name: an inverted MeSH heading yields its head noun
headCases.label: Burnout, Professional

headCases.name: a multi-part inversion still heads on the first comma
headCases.label: Aged, 80 and over

headCases.name: an uninverted heading has no head
headCases.label: Mindfulness

headCases.name: a parenthetical qualifier is stripped before heading
headCases.label: Depression (Psychology)

crosswalkCases.name: an exact label match is strong
ERIC's parenthetical qualifier still counts as the same label
an inverted MeSH heading matches ERIC's head noun, but only as possible
a synonym match explains that ERIC FOLDS the concept in — the Mindfulness trap

expected.evidenceMatches: folds this concept INTO that descriptor

crosswalkCases.name: a medical heading folded into a vague ERIC descriptor is still only likely
a MeSH entry term that is an ERIC descriptor in its own right

crosswalkCases.name: a MeSH entry term appearing as an ERIC synonym is the weakest signal
no candidate is a real answer, not a failure
one descriptor appears once, at its strongest tier
